intro.title: box-sizing: border-box
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with two colored boxes to visually understand how CSS calculates element sizes. You will learn the core concept of the CSS `box-sizing` property, specifically the `border-box` value, which changes how an element's width and height are calculated to include padding and borders. The main technology involved is CSS, using properties like `width`, `height`, `padding`, `border`, and `box-sizing`. By the end, you'll know how to apply `box-sizing: border-box` to make layout sizing more predictable and intuitive, a common practice in web development.
intro.usecase: The box-sizing: border-box property is essential for creating predictable, pixel-perfect layouts in real-world interfaces. Developers use it extensively when building form controls, dashboard panels, and card-based components where consistent dimensions are critical. For example, when creating a responsive grid of product cards in an e-commerce site, border-box ensures that padding and borders don't unexpectedly expand elements beyond their specified widths. This prevents layout shifts and alignment issues in complex UI systems like admin dashboards, data tables, and modal dialogs.
